page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a general-purpose server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Geekbench single-core and image processing scores fall into the strong category, as does the PassMark memory score. Multi-core and multi-threaded operations, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, perform in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 89.11 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 45.67 GB/sec.

This hardware configuration delivers balanced resource density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without the premium of specialized compute or memory-heavy instances. It is highly capable for text processing and small-scale language model inference, where it achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 443.84 tokens/sec for a 135M parameter model. The server is suited for general-purpose workloads, medium database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
